title: Weighted Average Call Money Rate
description: Volume-weighted average rate on overnight call money (inter-bank, uncollateralised) trades, per cent, daily, with traded volume (one leg, Rs. crore). It sits near the repo rate when liquidity is balanced, rises above it in deficit and falls toward the SDF rate in surplus, so it is a timely read on money-market tightness. HISTORY IS SHORT: recorded from CCIL's published money-market rates (which match RBI's Money Market Operations release), starting 2026-10-28; the series grows with each run and is not a full historical series.
source: CCIL (Clearing Corporation of India), money-market rates; cross-checked to RBI Money Market Operations

qna.question: What is the call money rate?
qna.answer: The call market is the overnight, uncollateralised inter-bank market. The weighted average rate is the volume-weighted mean of the day's trades; the volume is the one-leg amount traded in Rs. crore.^Most overnight money-market activity is now collateralised (triparty repo), so call volumes are small relative to total overnight volume.

qna.question: How should I read it?
qna.answer: Compare with the repo rate and the SDF/MSF corridor. A call rate above the repo rate points to tight liquidity; one near the SDF rate points to surplus. Daily spikes around reserve-requirement and tax-payment dates are common.^Pair with the net LAF series on this dashboard.

qna.question: Caveats?
qna.answer: History begins on 2026-10-28 because the source pages show only the latest days; the dashboard adds each new day as it is published, so the series is short for now.^CCIL reports four decimals; the RBI release rounds to two (for example 5.5772 versus 5.58).

note: Accumulating series: history starts 2026-10-28 and grows with each run.
